device.name: Tuya-Based Smart Device (Smart Life / white-label IoT)
device.notes:
Tuya is the IoT platform behind an enormous fraction of inexpensive white-label smart plugs, bulbs, switches, sensors and IR blasters — sold under hundreds of brand names and driven by the "Smart Life" / "Tuya Smart" apps. Every Tuya device beacons a small, self-describing UDP datagram to the broadcast address roughly every ten seconds: on port 6666 for protocol version 3.1 (plaintext JSON) and on port 6667 for 3.2+ (the same JSON under AES-128-ECB). It is a discovery beacon, NOT a control channel.
This project DISCOVERS Tuya devices and identifies them; it does not drive them. Local control (the 0x55aa command protocol on TCP 6668) requires the device's per-device LOCAL KEY — a secret Tuya issues to the vendor's app via its cloud — which this project does not have and does not ask for. So we read the beacon, show a generic smart-device pictogram, and tell the user the device is set up and controlled through its own app. There is no local web admin UI on a Tuya device, so no admin_url is offered.
THE BEACON. Frame: prefix 00 00 55 aa, u32 sequence, u32 command (0x00 on 6666, 0x13 on 6667), u32 payload length, then the payload — an optional 4-byte return code, the data (plaintext JSON on 6666; ciphertext on 6667), a u32 CRC32 and the suffix 00 00 aa 55. The 6667 cipher is AES-128-ECB under a SINGLE key shared by every Tuya device on earth: md5 of the ASCII string "yGAdlopoPVldABfn". That key is published in every open Tuya library and is a DISCOVERY key only — it unwraps the beacon a device already broadcasts to the whole segment; it is NOT the per-device local key that protects control. Useful fields in the JSON: gwId (the stable device id — the good identity key, survives a DHCP move), ip (the device's own address), version (protocol, e.g. "3.3") and productKey (identifies the firmware product, shared across a model). The device's address is the beacon's source IP (or the ip field, which the device is authoritative about).
Because Tuya is a platform, the beacon does not name a device CATEGORY — productKey identifies a firmware build, not "plug" vs "bulb" — so the pictogram is the generic smart-device glyph rather than a guessed type, and the category is "other".

credentials.notes: Identify-only: no credential crosses to this app. The fixed broadcast key that unwraps the 6667 beacon is a published discovery constant, not a device secret; the per-device local key that would permit control is never obtained or stored.

factory_reset.description: Two routes, and the app one is worth knowing about because it is not obviously a factory reset from its name: the vendor app's "Restore Factory Defaults" and its "Remove Device" sit next to each other in the same menu and do different amounts of damage. The physical gesture differs per product — commonly a button held or a power-cycle pattern — and belongs in that product's own documentation rather than here.
factory_reset.effect: Removes the device from the Tuya account's device list and erases all of its data, returning it to pairing mode. It clears nothing this spec's consumers store — this entry only identifies the device — but it does invalidate any local key already extracted for it, so anything controlling the device locally stops working.

procedures.basis: The Tuya Smart / Smart Life app user manual, which distinguishes this from the adjacent Remove Device action.
procedures.name: Restore Factory Defaults from the vendor app

steps.action: Open the device in the vendor app and choose Restore Factory Defaults.
steps.expect: The device is removed from the device list and all of its data is erased; it returns to pairing mode and its local key is invalidated.

procedures.basis: The pattern across Tuya OEM products — a button held, or a power-cycle sequence — rather than documentation for any one device. Consult the specific product's manual.
procedures.name: The product's own physical reset gesture

steps.action: Perform the reset gesture documented for the specific product.
steps.expect: The device returns to advertising or broadcasting in pairing mode.

methods.description: The device is already on the LAN; discovery is the passive UDP 6666/6667 beacon.

steps.action: Listen on UDP 6666 (plaintext) and 6667 (AES-128-ECB under md5("yGAdlopoPVldABfn")).
steps.expect: A beacon carrying gwId, ip, version and productKey; the device's address is the source IP.

steps.action: Show the smart-device pictogram; direct the user to the device's own app for control (no local admin UI, no local key held).

setup.notes: Nothing to set up for identification: listen on UDP 6666/6667, read (and for 6667 decrypt with the fixed key) the beacon, show the smart-device pictogram and note that the device is managed in its own app. Confidence high: verified live and the frame/key are the published, authoritative ecosystem constants.

rejoin.notes: Stays discoverable by its UDP beacon wherever it sits on the LAN; identity keys on gwId, not IP, so a DHCP move does not lose it.

testing.notes: Tuya discovery verified live 2026-08-16: a real device on the segment beaconed the encrypted (6667) datagram every ~10 s; decrypting it with the fixed broadcast key md5("yGAdlopoPVldABfn") (AES-128-ECB) yielded the self-description {"ip":..., "gwId":"03712560…", "version":"3.3", "productKey":"…", "active":2, "encrypt":true}, confirming the frame layout (prefix 00 00 55 aa, optional return code, ciphertext, CRC, suffix 00 00 aa 55) and the field mapping. Identify-only: no control channel is opened — the per-device local key is not held — so the app shows a pictogram and a "set up in the vendor app" note. The Rust core's Tuya decrypt is covered by a round-trip unit test that builds its own frame.

local_access.summary: Locally controllable in principle (the 0x55aa protocol on TCP 6668) but ONLY with the device's per-device local key, a secret issued through the Tuya cloud to the vendor's app. This project does not hold that key and deliberately scopes Tuya to identify-only, handing control to the device's own app. Third-party local control (tinytuya, localtuya, ESPHome/ Tasmota reflashing) exists but is out of scope here.
